text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Conservation group Norges Naturvernforbund and the Centre Party have criticised the government for not giving financial support to wind energy projects. Terje Kronen, head of Norges Naturvernforbund, says the government of Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland is too little interested in renewable energy sources and too focused on gas-fired power stations.

- Statoil is today raising gasoline prices by 0.10 crowns per litre and it is likely that others will soon follow. Statoil says the rise is due to increasing costs following a stronger dollar and higher gasoline prices on the international market. Statoil and Esso, the two largest retail gasoline sellers, are losing market share, while sales at Shell, Hydro Texaco and Fina are rising.
- Only two Norwegian companies, Norsk Hydro and Orkla, have been included in a new European share index, the FTSE Eurotop 300.

- A strengthening of the dollar exchange rate against the crown has lifted Norway's oil revenues by five billion crowns so far this year. Oil prices in 1997 have been around 10 crowns higher than the government's estimate in the 1997 budget.

- Anne Thidemann, president of the Norwegian Athletics Association, will meet officials from the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) in Athens on Tuesday. IAAF officials on Monday said Norway would be banned from the sport if it failed to report positive drugs tests on time.

- Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg wants to put value-added tax (VAT) on all services and newspapers. The extra VAT would bolster state earnings by eight to nine billion crowns, but the government also will reduce the VAT rate by two percentage points, such that the state's income will remain unchanged.

- Braathens SAFE and Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) say tickets will rise by 25 percent if the government slaps VAT on flights. The airlines say flights on uneconomical domestic routes also would be reduced by around 25 percent if the extra tax comes into force.
- American investment bank Chase Manhatten Bank has increased its shareholding in Narvesen group, the kiosk chain, and is now the sixth largest shareholder.
